sampling_model.design: A two-arm randomized vaccine trial is combined with an external exposure-surveillance sample from the same period-specific target environment.
sampling_model.units: For each trial arm, conditional on that arm's own realized total, the mutually exclusive categories consisting of no first infection and first infection by period and variant have the stated multinomial law. For each period-specific external total, exposure counts on \(\mathcal V_0\) have the stated multinomial law. No independence among the two trial-arm blocks and two external-period blocks is required: each block's exact error bound is first averaged over its own possibly random total, and a union bound gives simultaneous coverage unconditionally over the trial and external samples. No joint conditional coverage claim given the realized trial arm sizes is made.
sampling_model.treatment: \(A\in\{0,1\}\) has known probabilities \(\pi\), and the trial records the period and variant of each first infection.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment-arm positivity is standard. Noninfecting-exposure priming is indexed by the disclosed sensitivity value \(\delta\), with \(\delta=0\) giving no priming and \(\delta=1\) permitting unrestricted priming. Fiber-wide period-two vaccine reference-risk positivity is a separate novel, LP-checkable restriction used only for finite Charnes--Cooper endpoints; the extended identified set and exact projection allow zero denominators.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The trial and exposure cell probabilities are covered by exact likelihood-ratio-ordered multinomial inversions at Bonferroni level \(\alpha/4\) for each of two arms and two periods. At total count zero, \(T_p(0)=0\) and \(\Gamma_0(u;\gamma)=\Delta\), so zero-total and zero-cell samples require no correction. The simultaneous primitive confidence set is projected through every nonempty \(\mathcal P_\delta(b',q',\omega)\) fiber; the same primitive event covers the union over the prespecified \(\mathcal D\). The construction does not studentize or select an endpoint optimizer.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 derives sharp two-period bounds for a single-pathogen challenge effect from conventional vaccine-trial risks.
Section 4 shows that multi-variant vaccine-effectiveness measures can be time-varying under leaky and all-or-none mechanisms.
The weighted estimating-equation model permits time-varying vaccine efficacy and time-varying pathogen distributions under a marked exposure process.
Case-only strain odds ratios receive a biological relative-efficacy interpretation under stated exposure and susceptibility conditions.
Theorems 1 through 3 identify conditional relative strain efficacy from case-only data under explicit missingness and causal assumptions.
Finite latent response types and linear programming yield tight treatment-effect bounds and attaining distributions.
The paper constructs random regions with uniform asymptotic coverage of an entire identified set or its known image.
Calibrated bootstrap projection gives uniformly valid intervals for smooth functions of moment-constrained partially identified parameters.
Derivative-aware resampling is valid for directionally differentiable maps in settings where the ordinary bootstrap can fail.
The paper develops a powerful single-pathogen test of treatment-effect constancy and additional waning bounds.

Section 5 defines the marginal time-to-event challenge subtype effect, and the marginal-identification proposition identifies it as a ratio of two observed cause-specific hazard ratios under the paper's stated time-to-event identification and proportionality assumptions.

body.tldr: Changing pathogen variants make early-versus-late vaccine challenge risk depend on one latent coupling of exposures and responses across periods. The response type permits a noninfecting period-one exposure to alter later controlled susceptibility, and a disclosed \(\delta\in[0,1]\) bounds the altered fraction. Pointwise in \(\delta\), a finite common-history polytope exactly represents every compatible law, its extended reference-mixture ratio set is sharp, reciprocal endpoints are attained under the separate denominator condition, and a common-law dual certifies strict signs. For \(K=2\), finitely many linear programs recover the exact affine hull of the positive comparison face, and a quadratic cross-product test is necessary and sufficient for the Perényi--Stensrud controlled-risk contrast to be constant and equal its observed-hazard counterpart; empty, nonconstant, and constant-mismatch cases have explicit certificates. Exact multinomial inversion, with \(\Gamma_0(u;\gamma)=\Delta\), gives unconditional whole-set coverage after projection through every nonempty fiber and through the prespecified \(\delta\)-envelope, without independence across sampling blocks or a conditional-on-realized-arm-sizes claim.

project_justification.gap: Janvin and Stensrud (2025) give sharp single-pathogen challenge-effect bounds, and Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5) identify a variant-specific time-to-event challenge subtype effect under exposure and proportionality restrictions. Neither gives a sharp common-history ratio set from trial first-infection risks plus external variant-exposure margins when a prior exposure that did not infect may alter later controlled susceptibility, nor an observable sign certificate valid pointwise over a disclosed bound on that priming.
project_justification.niche: The target compares one policy-fixed reference mixture across periods and defines period-two challenge risk after no period-one exposure. A history-indexed response array separates that target response from the response after a noninfecting exposure; the linear sensitivity value \(\delta\) then restricts their disagreement without replacing external exposure margins by selected case-strain frequencies. Routine negative tests and serial serology do not justify a small \(\delta\), so analysis without a controlled validation substudy spans \(\mathcal D=[0,1]\).
project_justification.fill: The substantive chain supplies, pointwise in \(\delta\), exact common-history compression, an always-defined extended sharp set, finite attained reciprocal endpoints under the disclosed denominator condition, and a common-law sign dual with compatible counterlaws. For \(K=2\), the collapse boundary is computed by a positive-face linear program, linear programs for the exact affine hull, and a quadratic identity test; its failures yield an infeasibility certificate, two compatible laws with different controlled-risk contrasts, or one compatible-law observable-mismatch witness. Exact primitive-cell multinomial inversion defines \(\Gamma_0(u;\gamma)=\Delta\) at zero total count and projects the simultaneous primitive confidence event through every nonempty fixed-\(\delta\) fiber and the prespecified sensitivity envelope, yielding unconditional whole-set coverage. Case-frequency substitution and the fixed-fiber policy-mixture radius remain separate questions.

body.related_work: Janvin and Stensrud (2025, Theorem 1 and Appendix B) establish sharp finite single-pathogen two-period challenge-effect bounds and attaining laws; their multiple-version analysis does not retain external period-specific variant margins or index later controlled response by a prior noninfecting exposure. Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5 and the marginal \(CSE_k\) identification proposition) identify a time-to-event challenge subtype effect from observed cause-specific hazards under time-to-event exchangeability, positivity, consistency, exposure necessity, no cross-infectivity, a covariate-invariant exposure ratio, and scaled-new-infection proportionality. Here their controlled-risk coordinates are represented by \(\rho_{ta}(x,e^{(v)})\), with the period-two coordinate based on \(R^{[0]}_{2av}\); instead of asserting class inclusion, the exact boundary is the vanishing of a computable quadratic cross-product on the LP-computed affine hull of the positive common-history face. Tomer and Biccler (2022) analyze temporal movement under specified competing-variant mechanisms. Follmann and Huang (2018), Gilbert et al. (2001), Edlefsen (2014), and van der Laan and Gilbert (2023) motivate why selected infecting strains require extra exposure and susceptibility restrictions, so case frequencies are not substituted for the external margins \(q\). Balke and Pearl (1997) inform the finite response-type lift. Romano and Shaikh (2010) and Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) inform whole-set projection; the present construction uses exact multinomial inversion including the zero-total definition \(\Gamma_0(u;\gamma)=\Delta\), obtains simultaneous coverage by a union bound without block independence, and projects the resulting event through all nonempty fibers and the prespecified sensitivity envelope.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The parameter \(\delta\) controls whether a single period-one exposure that did not infect changes the period-two controlled response relative to no prior exposure. Routine negative tests establish noninfection, not absence of immune priming, and serial serology need not detect response-relevant cellular or mucosal changes; neither identifies a small \(\delta\). Without a randomized or controlled validation substudy, the honest sensitivity range is \(\mathcal D=[0,1]\). The finite map still abstracts from multiple distinct noninfecting exposures within one period.
body.honest_scope: Exact common-history projection, the unconditional extended sharp set, finite attained reciprocal endpoints under the separately disclosed fiber-wide denominator condition, and common-history sign separation are substantive claims pointwise in prespecified \(\delta\). The target period-two risk uses \(R^{[0]}_{21v}\), while observed period-two infections use \(R^{[H_1]}_{2av}\); their discrepancy among noninfected exposees is bounded, not suppressed. For \(K=2\), collapse to the observed hazard contrast holds exactly when observed positivity and positive controlled-risk-face feasibility hold, the quadratic cross-product vanishes on the exact affine hull, and its constant equals the observed value. Failure of observed positivity makes that comparison undefined and is not an empty-face certificate. The exact multinomial confidence projection covers the full sharp fixed-\(\delta\) set, and the same unconditional event covers its prespecified \(\mathcal D\)-envelope; it makes no conditional coverage claim given realized arm sizes and uses no independence among count blocks. Fiber infeasibility is failure and never vacuous positivity. External exposure margins remain primitives; pooled case-strain frequencies do not replace them.
